newsitem.title: FRANCE: Canal Plus files suit over Monarchy dea.
newsitem.headline: Canal Plus files suit over Monarchy dea.

text.p: French pay-television group Canal Plus said on Thursday that it had filed suit in the Paris Commercial Court to obtain the forced execution of a contract it signed with Monarchy Entrerprises about New Regency films.

Canal Plus said it had reached an agreement in June 1996 for the exclusive French pay television rights for Regency film productions. This was subject to certain conditions which had meanwhile been met.
However, Monarchy in early 1997 signed another deal with Canal Plus' rival TPS (Television par Satellite) and film rights company TCM.
TPS is a joint venture of TF1, Lyonnaise des Eaux , France Television, France Telecom and Luxembourg's CLT.

"TPS was informed of the existence of the agreement between Monarchy and Canal Plus and in fact received a copy of a letter dated April 29, 1997, in which Canal Plus insisted that Monarchy honour the deal that had been reached with Canal Plus," Canal Plus said in a statement.
